abstract:
Delete a set $S$ of primes of density exponent $\alpha\in(1/2,1)$ from the Euler product of $\zeta$, and let $\beta(S)$ be the error exponent of the $S$-free integers. Random and regular deletions satisfy $\beta(S)\ge\alpha/2$ (rStation Papers 116 and 118). Whether some deletion has $\beta(S)<\alpha/2$ (the *corner*) is open. We show that, in the two pure cases below, a corner set must have zeros of its own in every window of polylogarithmic height; the mixed case is left open. Write $\zeta_{\mathcal P'}=\zeta F_S$ with $F_S(s)=\prod_{p\in S}(1-p^{-s})$.
- If $\zeta_{\mathcal P'}$ keeps every zero of $\zeta$ with its multiplicity, then, under RH, $F_S$ has a zero with real part at least $\alpha/2-\eta$ in every such window. Without RH the same holds outside a sparse exceptional set of windows.
- If $\zeta_{\mathcal P'}$ keeps none of them, then, unconditionally, $\zeta_{\mathcal P'}$ has zeros with real part at least $1/2-\eta$ in every such window, none of them zeros of $\zeta$.

Under RH we also extend the regular-set barrier of Paper 116 (Thm 4) to every admissible density profile. As an example, Seip's sparse sets with even multiplicity continue analytically past $\alpha/2$, yet under RH they still satisfy $\beta\ge\alpha/2$. So continuation past $\alpha/2$ does not by itself give the corner; in our arguments the obstruction is growth. Finally, the number of zeros forced here ($\gg T(\log T)^{-C}$ up to height $T$) is compatible with the number the corner hypothesis allows ($\ll T\log T$), so these counts alone do not close the argument. We explain why a pointwise rigidity input for zeros near the critical line of $F_S$, of the kind the functional equation supplies for $\zeta$, appears to be needed. The paper does not decide the corner and makes no claim about the Riemann hypothesis.

change_summary:
v2 makes the five clarifications the v1 review requested. Theorem 2 now states as (ii) the capacity estimate that v1 proved inside its proof, with its strict inequality and conditions (σ < κ/2 − η, A(η − ε) > 1); (i) is unchanged. No other theorem changes.

1. **Theorem 2 versus Theorem 1.** New Remark 5.3: (i) location also follows from Theorem 1 at σ' = κ/2 − η, with windows of the same order. §5 adds (ii) capacity: on the line σ, zeros with real part ≤ κ/2 − η absorb only o(diagonal). No advantage in window size or zero counts is claimed.

2. **Theorem 3.** "Verbatim" is replaced by the adaptations of [1, Thm 4(b)]: Lemma 16(iii) needs only the discrepancy bound and |c_p| ≤ 1. Lemma 17(b),(c) are replaced by the hypotheses. In Lemma 18, π_p ≤ 1/2 gives c_p² ≥ 1/4 on all of S. The counting hypothesis gives V_X ≥ X^{α−2σ−o(1)}, which suffices.

3. **Contour statements.** §3.2 derives the cut identity (positively oriented slit rectangle, jump 2πi·m_z of the logarithm at each cut, horizontals at Lemma H heights); poles have m_z < 0, giving −P_σ. Lemma 4.1 gives an explicit B_far: (a) B_far = o(diagonal), which the proofs use; (b) B_far ≤ X^{−1} for larger N. Step 4 records Z_near ≤ −(1−o(1))ŵ(0)V^{1/2}, and Remark 4.3 adds its far-zero condition. Lemma H is applied to ζ_P′ in case A (ord F_S ≤ ord ζ_P′ there), so counting zeros of F_S needs no RH.

4. **§4.4.** Worded via n_ρ. F_S has poles where ζ_P' does not keep the full multiplicity of a zero of ζ; zeros kept by ζ_P' are the possible inherited zeros.

5. **Presentation.** Numbered references; check-status notes moved to the Acknowledgements; the numerical supplement cited in §3.2 (scope: bookkeeping only).
title: Prime deletions that beat the square-root barrier need zeros of their own
